2026-12-15.title: Tuesday of the Third Week of Advent
readings: I will leave in the midst of you a people humble and lowly
The Lord hears the cry of the poor
The tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him
2026-12-15.verse: For John came to you in the way of righteousness and you did not believe him, but the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him; and even after you saw it, you did not change your minds and believe him.
theo: Zephaniah condemns a proud city that “has listened to no voice” and promises a different future: God will purify the lips of the peoples, and “I will leave in the midst of you a people humble and lowly. They shall seek refuge in the name of the LORD.” This humble remnant is the true Israel of Advent: Mary, Joseph, Zechariah, Elizabeth, the shepherds.

Jesus tells of two sons. One refuses to work in the vineyard but later changes his mind and goes; the other says yes but does not go. The religious leaders gave God many words; tax collectors and prostitutes gave him their repentance. “Even after you saw it, you did not change your minds.” Advent asks not for fine words but for a changed heart. It is never too late to turn and go into the vineyard.
outline: Ask: are you a “yes, Lord” person who never goes?
Point 1 · A humble and lowly people
God builds his future with the humble.
The son who changed his mind did the Father's will.
Repentance opens the door of the Kingdom.
“They shall seek refuge in the name of the Lord.”
live: Turn a no into a yes (Matthew 21:29)
Do something you refused God earlier.
Let someone else have the credit today.
2026-12-15.prayer: Lord, the poor cry out and you hear them. Make me humble and lowly, change my heart where I have said no to you, and let my yes be more than words. Amen.
altar: At Mass we say Amen. This Advent, let our Amen at Communion become a yes that we carry into our lives.

quick: God's future belongs to the humble remnant.
Repentant sinners enter the Kingdom first.
2026-12-15.action: Do something you earlier refused God.
2026-12-15.question: Is my “yes” to God only words?

family.explain: One son said no but then obeyed. The other said yes but did not go. Jesus wants us to do what we say.
family.intention: We pray that we may keep our promises to God and to each other.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there something we said we would do but haven't done yet?”

pm.open: Lord God, you love the humble and lowly. As we gather, help us to change our minds and do your will, not only with words but with our lives. Amen.
share: Which son am I most like (Matthew 21:28–31)?
Where have I said yes to God but not acted?
Zephaniah speaks of a humble people (Zephaniah 3:12). What would humility look like in my life today?
pm.resp: Lord, we will do your will.
interc: For the Church, that she may be humble and lowly, seeking refuge in the Lord.
For sinners, that they may change their minds and return to God.
For those who keep faith only in words, that their lives may match their lips.
For the poor of the Lord, who wait for his coming.
For our group, that we may keep our promises.
pm.close: Lord God, you welcome the repentant sinner. Make our yes to you sincere, and count us among the humble who wait for your Son. Amen.

illus: A man in Kollam had promised his dying mother that he would return to the sacraments. For years he said, “Soon.” One Advent, reading this Gospel, he realised he was the second son. That Saturday he went to confession.

homily: Dear friends, the prophet Zephaniah speaks of a city that is rebellious and defiled: it has listened to no voice, it has accepted no correction (Zephaniah 3:1–2). Then God promises: I will leave in the midst of you a people humble and lowly. They shall seek refuge in the name of the Lord (Zephaniah 3:12).
God's future belongs to the humble: the anawim, the poor of the Lord. Mary, Joseph, the shepherds, Simeon and Anna belong to this humble remnant who waited for the Messiah.

In the Gospel Jesus tells a parable. A man has two sons. He asks the first to work in the vineyard; he says, I will not, but later changes his mind and goes. He asks the second; he says, I go, sir, but does not go. Which of the two did the will of his father? (Matthew 21:28–31).

Then Jesus says something shocking to the religious leaders: the tax collectors and prostitutes are going into the kingdom of God ahead of you. For John came in the way of righteousness, and they believed him, but you did not (Matthew 21:31–32).

The second son represents those who say yes with their lips but no with their lives. The first son represents sinners who first say no but then repent. Both are in us. We say yes at Mass, then no at home. We refuse God, and then, by grace, we change our minds.

It is never too late to change our minds. This Advent, let us be the son who repents. Let us look honestly at where we have said yes but not gone, and go now. And let us ask to belong to the humble remnant who seek refuge in the Lord. Amen.
kids: Children, one son said no but then obeyed; the other said yes but did not. Jesus wants us to say yes and then really do it!

intro: God's humble remnant, the son who changed his mind, sinners who believed.

sub: The proud city listened to no voice.
They take refuge in his name.
q: For I will leave in the midst of you a people humble and lowly. They shall seek refuge in the name of the LORD.
For the Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy is his name.
points.apply: Let someone else have the credit today.

sub: One son said no, then went.
The other said yes and did not go.
God wants deeds, not just words.
q: The Lord said: Because these people draw near with their mouths and honor me with their lips, while their hearts are far from me, and their worship of me is a human commandment learned by rote.
Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only the one who does the will of my Father in heaven.
points.apply: Turn one “no” to God into a “yes” today.

sub: Tax collectors and prostitutes believed John.
The leaders saw and did not repent.
It is never too late to turn.
q: The LORD is near to the brokenhearted, and saves the crushed in spirit.

For John came to you in the way of righteousness and you did not believe him, but the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him; and even after you saw it, you did not change your minds and believe him.
